text: The daemon reads a line from the socket, strips the framing, and hands the text to the engine. If the engine is busy, the request waits its turn; otherwise it starts at once! Does anyone really read these logs at 3.5 seconds per line? Probably not, but we keep them anyway, because one day somebody will need to know why foo_bar() returned early; that day is always a bad one. Version 2.0 of the protocol adds a header, a checksum, and a small amount of optimism... It also adds a very long clause that keeps going without any punctuation at all, so that the splitter has to fall back to something smaller than a sentence, and decide where to cut it, for the model to cope with it gracefully, and then there is the end of it.
